camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: There were lovely old trees all along the road, we saw lots of buffalo (enormous) pulling carts, and quite a few camels.

camel.speaker: D
camel.excerpt: Helena and I saw some little camel-bone cocktail sticks, with two elephants carved on one end, they were only 1 rupee (7p) each.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: Then we went to a bazaar and got some really spicy meatballs.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: In the morning, Mum, Dad & I went to the Bazaar, Colin had a terrible sore through, so he stayed in bed.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We walked round the bazaar, H & I looked at lots of Bangles, I saw some new Mascara jars which looked as though they were being sold with Mascara.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: Then we went to the bazaar, there were lots of bangles; some were glass, and had lovely colours that mixed and twisted beautifully.

bazaar.speaker: H
bazaar.excerpt: In the afternoon, we all visited a Bazaar.

bazaar.speaker: D
bazaar.excerpt: We went round the ‘Kashmir’ Bazaar, actually, it was all copper and things, across the road was thge jewellery bazaar, it had some beautiful gold bracelets etc.

bazaar.speaker: F
bazaar.excerpt: We went to the copper bazaar.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: We got up fairly early and went to see the big Mosque, supposed to be the biggest in the world, built by the last of the great Moghuls.

mosque.speaker: D
mosque.excerpt: Unlike the Persian Mosques, which had styles, it was lots of carved Marble etc.

mosque.speaker: F
mosque.excerpt: We went to a big mosque.

mosque.speaker: H
mosque.excerpt: We did a speedy getaway and went to the Mosque.

colin.speaker: D
colin.excerpt: In the morning, Mum, Dad & I went to the Bazaar, Colin had a terrible sore through, so he stayed in bed.

colin.speaker: D
colin.excerpt: We drove to ‘Dana’, it was a tribal area, all the shops, other than food and medicinal shops, made and/or sold guns, we had an interesting time with Colin, who knows lots about guns.

colin.speaker: D
colin.excerpt: We got back to Peshawar and said goodby to Colin.

colin.speaker: H
colin.excerpt: After visiting Darra which has lots of little shops which make and sell all kinds of guns, pistols etc we drove back to Peshawar and left Colin there.

snake.speaker: D
snake.excerpt: We went to see some more ruins, the first had very smooth rounded walls, we found some small snake skins, then Dad found one that was over 5 feet long!

snake.speaker: F
snake.excerpt: Dad found a snake skin about 5 feet long!

snake.speaker: H
snake.excerpt: F and I went back to fetch the camera, meanwhile Dad found a small dried snake skin and a huge one more that was as long as 5 feet.

gun.speaker: D
gun.excerpt: We saw lots of shops selling gun holsters etc..

gun.speaker: D
gun.excerpt: We drove to ‘Dana’, it was a tribal area, all the shops, other than food and medicinal shops, made and/or sold guns, we had an interesting time with Colin, who knows lots about guns.

gun.speaker: F
gun.excerpt: We have been to a gun market.

gun.speaker: F
gun.excerpt: There were some nice rifles: they were heavier than I expected.

gun.speaker: F
gun.excerpt: What I liked was a small 0.22 automatic pistol.

gun.speaker: F
gun.excerpt: All of the guns were made in small shops with primitive tools, not in big factories.

gun.speaker: H
gun.excerpt: After visiting Darra which has lots of little shops which make and sell all kinds of guns, pistols etc we drove back to Peshawar and left Colin there.

gun.speaker: D
gun.excerpt: We went to visit the Museum, near the Museum was a big Gun (Cannon) called Zamzama, it was very old.

chipmunk.speaker: D
chipmunk.excerpt: (Shalimar had the Tahj-Mahal built as well) it was very beautiful with lots of green parrots and chipmunks.

chipmunk.speaker: F
chipmunk.excerpt: Then we went to some gardens; they had some nice green parrots and chipmunks.

chipmunk.speaker: F
chipmunk.excerpt: The chipmunks had lovely bushy grey tails and white stripes.

chipmunk.speaker: H
chipmunk.excerpt: Soon we went to some very famous gardens where there were lots of chipmunks in the trees.

chipmunk.speaker: H
chipmunk.excerpt: The chipmunks had two brown stripes, a white belly and a very bushy tail and fur all over.

museum.speaker: D
museum.excerpt: In the morning, we went to Peshawar Museum, there were lots of Buddah things there.

museum.speaker: F
museum.excerpt: We went to the Peshawar Museum.

museum.speaker: D
museum.excerpt: We decided to sleep at the Resthouse, first we looked at the museum, and then at ??

museum.speaker: H
museum.excerpt: At Taxila, we went to the Museum where there were lots of Buddhist statues.

museum.speaker: D
museum.excerpt: At Raul-Pindi we visited the Army Museum, it had some quite interesting things there, from places we’ve been, or are going to.

museum.speaker: F
museum.excerpt: Then we went to the Army museum; there were some nice suits of chainmail.

museum.speaker: H
museum.excerpt: We drove to Rawalpindi and visited the Army Museum.

museum.speaker: D
museum.excerpt: We went to visit the Museum, near the Museum was a big Gun (Cannon) called Zamzama, it was very old.

museum.speaker: D
museum.excerpt: In the Museum, were some interesting little scenes with figures etc made of clay, there were rice grinders, a pottery factory and lacquer workshop, as well as Hindu and Muslim Marriage processions etc, and people on the streets.

museum.speaker: H
museum.excerpt: When Mum, Dad and D came back, we drove to the Museum where there were some clay models of weavers, potters, rice grinders, untouchables, and others who I did not look at.

museum.speaker: F
museum.excerpt: There were lots of small models of Zamzam, the big cannon near the museum.

mascara.speaker: D
mascara.excerpt: There were some beautiful Chinese things as well, in one of the rooms, I saw some Mascara jars, none as nice as mine though.

mascara.speaker: D
mascara.excerpt: We walked round the bazaar, H & I looked at lots of Bangles, I saw some new Mascara jars which looked as though they were being sold with Mascara.

tikka.speaker: D
tikka.excerpt: Then we went and walked round a few streets, we bought some ‘Tikkas’, which were like Hamburgers, but VERY hot and spicy.

tikka.speaker: D
tikka.excerpt: We bought some Tikkas (very small, unfortunately) and some Chapatties (bread).

gruel.speaker: H
gruel.excerpt: For breakfast, we had gruel (which F and I liked).
